notes: Scores and latencies are provisional until the benchmark reruns (spec 18). kind is asr (speech recognition), cleanup (tidying a dictated sentence) or compose (writing text from a spoken instruction); a compose entry may name the same files as a cleanup entry, in which case it is the same weights judged for a different job, it is installed exactly when that cleanup model is, and it costs no extra bytes. The compose scores are a judgement carried over from the cleanup benchmark, not a measurement, and a writing benchmark is still missing. languages maps a language code to a quality score from 0 to 100; an absent code means unsupported, and the key * scores every other language the runtime supports without a measurement. hardware maps gpu and cpu to the estimated milliseconds for a 15 s dictation (release to text for asr, the cleanup call for cleanup, one composed email of 150 to 300 tokens for compose), null when the model cannot run there at all; for compose a large number does not disqualify a model, only null does. size_bytes counts file plus extra_files, and an install of the app plus both engine folders plus every model one machine needs must stay at or below 5,000,000,000 bytes (spells.modelcatalog.INSTALL_BUDGET_BYTES, spec 19.4). engine_args may name an extra file as {extra:N}, which the engine supervisor replaces with that file's absolute path. redistributable false keeps a model out of the installer. CPU numbers were measured on an i7-14700K without its discrete GPU, with every engine pinned to one logical processor per performance core at 8 threads; the cleanup numbers used the CPU build. GPU numbers are estimates, not measurements.

models.notes: Provisional. Scores are 100 times one minus the word error rate on the synthetic plus Common Voice clips: en 0.13, de 0.15, sq 0.52, so Albanian recognition is poor. Other languages are not measured. CPU: about 4.5 s with full context, pinned to the performance cores (encode 3.1 s). GPU: treated as fast; the reference laptop (RTX 5060) measured 278 ms release to transcript on a 6 s clip with the tiny model.

Provisional. The speech model new installs get for English and German. Quantised to Q4_K_M on the desktop from the bf16 weights of Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B with llama.cpp b10997, since nobody else publishes this file; the installers download it from the models-v1 release of this project on GitHub. Served by llama-server with the same audio projector as the Q8_0 entry (ggml-org/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-GGUF). Word error rate on the long clips: en 0.079, de 0.120, the same as the Q8_0 file. It does not recognise Albanian. CPU: en 1125 ms and de 1185 ms median for a long clip on 8 pinned threads, against 1149 ms and 1267 ms for the Q8_0 file, measured once on the i7-14700K; 1150 is their rounded middle. GPU latency is an estimate carried over from the Q8_0 entry, not a measurement. It is 320,533,504 bytes smaller than the Q8_0 entry, which is what lets a processor with English, German and Albanian keep it next to Whisper inside the install budget.

Provisional. Served by llama-server with its audio projector (ggml-org/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-GGUF). Word error rate on the long clips: en 0.079, de 0.120. It does not recognise Albanian: every Albanian clip was reported as another language. CPU: about 1.2 s (en) to 1.4 s (de) for a long clip, pinned to the performance cores; the first request after loading takes about 3 s, which the warm-up absorbs. GPU latency is an estimate. No installer puts this file on a machine any more: the Q4_K_M entry above has the same word error rates, is faster on the processor and smaller, so a plan and a machine holding both choose it. This entry stays so that an install from before the change, which holds only this file, keeps choosing it.

Provisional. Flutra/whisper-large-v3-turbo-sq-v2 converted to q8_0. Word error rate on the synthetic Albanian clips 0.455 against 0.608 for the stock model; German gets worse (0.154 to 0.316) and English is unchanged. Its repository declares no licence, so it is for personal use only and never ships in the installer. GPU latency is an estimate.

Provisional. CPU median 1024 ms (English 714 ms) with the MTP draft head as the speculative decoder, slightly faster than the n-gram flags; both together were not faster. English and German excellent: fillers and self-corrections applied, meaning kept. Albanian safe but conservative: never damaged meaning, often left Albanian fillers and self-corrections in. GPU latency is an estimate.
Provisional. CPU median 2700 ms. English perfect, German very good. Albanian: best at applying self-corrections but occasionally changed a word (Cyrih became Zvicer). GPU latency is an estimate.
Provisional. CPU median 2160 ms. English and German excellent. Albanian harmful: translated Albanian into English twice (caught by the guards). GPU latency is an estimate.
Provisional. CPU median 1340 ms. English and German good. Albanian harmful: changed numbers. GPU latency is an estimate.
Provisional. CPU median 4050 ms. Albanian unsuitable: dropped half of a question. English and German were not judged separately in this run; their scores are placeholders. GPU latency is an estimate.

Provisional. The same file as the cleanup entry qwen3.5-4b-q4_k_m, judged for writing instead of cleaning. The writing scores are a judgement from the cleanup benchmark, not a measurement: it was the best writer of every model tried and the only one that applied Albanian self-corrections, so it leads in all three languages. A writing benchmark is still missing. The latencies are estimates for 150 to 300 written tokens, not measurements, and latency never disqualifies a compose model, because composing is not on the dictation latency path.

Provisional. The same file as the cleanup entry gemma-4-e2b-it-q4_0, judged for writing instead of cleaning, and the fallback writer whenever Qwen3.5 4B is not installed. The writing scores are a judgement from the cleanup benchmark, not a measurement: excellent at short English and German text, safe but cautious in Albanian, and a 2B model asked to write a whole email rather than to tidy one sentence, so every score sits below its cleanup score. A writing benchmark is still missing. The latencies are estimates for 150 to 300 written tokens.
